concepts.why: The patient's progressive dysarthria, dysphagia, cognitive impairment, and vertical gaze palsy, combined with the heterozygous pathogenic variant of the TBK1 gene, support this diagnosis.

concepts.preferred_label: Frontotemporal dementia and parkinsonism linked to TBK1

rationales.F01: Progressive dysarthria and dysphagia are non-specific symptoms that do not strongly point to any particular diagnosis.
rationales.F02: Cognitive impairment is a key feature of frontotemporal dementia and parkinsonism linked to TBK1, as well as frontotemporal lobar degeneration.
rationales.F03: Vertical gaze palsy is a characteristic feature of progressive supranuclear palsy.
rationales.F04: Tongue atrophy is a feature of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
rationales.F05: Pyramidal signs can be seen in a variety of conditions, including frontotemporal dementia and parkinsonism linked to TBK1 and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
rationales.F06: Severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia is a feature of Parkinson's disease and other parkinsonian disorders.
rationales.F07: Almost total loss in caudate nucleus is a feature of Parkinson's disease and other parkinsonian disorders.
rationales.F08: Low DAT binding measurements in the caudate nucleus are consistent with Parkinson's disease and other parkinsonian disorders.
rationales.F09: Low DAT binding measurements in the caudate nucleus are consistent with Parkinson's disease and other parkinsonian disorders.
rationales.F10: The presence of a heterozygous pathogenic variant of the TBK1 gene is highly suggestive of frontotemporal dementia and parkinsonism linked to TBK1.
rationales.F12: Large-amplitude, long-duration motor unit potentials are a feature of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
